case_studies.title: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Models across XPUs: Constraints and Acceleration for On-Robot Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are promising for generalist robot control, but on-robot deployment is bottlenecked by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. Most prior evaluations rely on desktop-grade GPUs, obscuring the trade-offs and opportunities offered by heterogeneous edge accelerators (GPUs/XPUs/NPUs). We present a systematic analysis for low-cost VLA deployment via model-hardware co-characterization. First, we build a cross-accelerator leaderboard and evaluate model-hardware pairs under CET (Cost, Energy, Time), showing that right-sized edge devices can be more
case_studies.summary: The problem of real-time inference in Vision-Language-Action models for on-robot deployment is addressed through a systematic analysis of model-hardware co-characterization. The AI approach involves building a cross-accelerator leaderboard to evaluate model-hardware pairs under various constraints, leading to the identification of right-sized edge devices for low-cost deployment. The outcome is a more efficient and cost-effective solution for VLA model deployment on robots.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can utilize the cross-accelerator leaderboard to evaluate and select the most suitable model-hardware pairs for their specific use case, considering factors such as cost, energy, and time. By doing so, they can optimize their VLA model deployment for on-robot applications and achieve better performance and efficiency.
case_studies.monetisation: The research presents a concrete business opportunity for companies developing robot control systems, as the optimized VLA model deployment can lead to significant cost savings and improved performance. This can be particularly relevant for industries such as robotics, manufacturing, and logistics, where autonomous robots are increasingly being used, and efficient control systems are crucial for their operation.

case_studies.title: AgentPulse: A Continuous Multi-Signal Framework for Evaluating AI Agents in Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Static benchmarks measure what AI agents can do at a fixed point in time but not how they are adopted, maintained, or experienced in deployment. We introduce AgentPulse, a continuous evaluation framework scoring 50 agents across 10 workload categories along four factors (Benchmark Performance, Adoption Signals, Community Sentiment, and Ecosystem Health) aggregated from 18 real-time signals across GitHub, package registries, IDE marketplaces, social platforms, and benchmark leaderboards. Three analyses ground the framework. The four factors capture largely complementary information (n=50; $ρ_{\
case_studies.summary: The current static benchmarks for evaluating AI agents have limitations as they only measure performance at a fixed point in time, neglecting how these agents are adopted, maintained, or experienced during deployment. The AgentPulse framework addresses this issue by continuously evaluating AI agents across multiple signals and factors, providing a more comprehensive assessment. By doing so, it captures a broader range of information, including adoption, community sentiment, and ecosystem health, thereby offering a more nuanced understanding of AI agent deployment.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from AgentPulse by incorporating continuous evaluation into their agent development workflows, utilizing real-time data from various sources to monitor and improve agent performance in deployment. This approach allows for more adaptive and responsive AI systems that can better meet the evolving needs of users and environments.
case_studies.monetisation: The AgentPulse framework presents a concrete business opportunity in the form of a subscription-based service that offers continuous evaluation and monitoring of AI agents for companies, providing them with actionable insights to enhance their AI-driven products and services. By leveraging the comprehensive assessment provided by AgentPulse, businesses can improve the reliability, efficiency, and overall value of their AI investments, leading to potential revenue growth and competitive advantage.

case_studies.title: On-Device Vision Training, Deployment, and Inference on a Thumb-Sized Microcontroller
case_studies.abstract: This paper presents a complete, end-to-end on-device vision machine learning pipeline, comprising data acquisition, two-layer CNN training with Adam optimization, and real-time inference, executing entirely on a microcontroller-class device costing $15-40 USD. Unlike cloud-based workflows that require external infrastructure and conceal the computational pipeline from the practitioner, this system implements every step of the core ML lifecycle in approximately 1,750 lines of readable C++ that compiles in under one minute using the Arduino IDE, with no external ML dependencies. case_studies.summary: The problem of relying on cloud-based workflows for machine learning tasks is addressed by developing an on-device vision machine learning pipeline. The AI approach involves implementing a two-layer CNN with Adam optimization on a microcontroller-class device, allowing for real-time inference and data acquisition. The outcome is a complete, end-to-end ML pipeline that can run on a low-cost device, reducing the need for external infrastructure.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this lesson by considering the use of microcontroller-class devices for on-device ML tasks, reducing latency and increasing efficiency. By leveraging the Arduino IDE and compiling C++ code, practitioners can develop and deploy ML models on low-cost devices, expanding the reach of AI applications.
case_studies.monetisation: The development of this on-device vision ML pipeline presents a concrete business opportunity for companies looking to create low-cost, edge-based AI solutions for various industries. By productizing this technology, companies can offer efficient and scalable AI solutions for applications such as smart home devices, wearables, or industrial automation, generating revenue through hardware sales or subscription-based services.

case_studies.title: Robustness Evaluation of a Foundation Segmentation Model Under Simulated Domain Shifts in Abdominal CT: Implications for Health Digital Twin Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Foundation segmentation models such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM) have demonstrated strong generalization across natural images; however, their robustness under clinically realistic medical imaging domain shifts remains insufficiently quantified. We present a systematic slice-level robustness audit of SAM (ViT-B) for spleen segmentation in abdominal CT using 1,051 nonempty slices from 41 volumes in the Medical Segmentation Decathlon. A standardized ground-truth-derived bounding-box protocol was used to isolate encoder robustness from prompt uncertainty. Controlled perturbations simulatin
case_studies.summary: The study evaluates the robustness of a foundation segmentation model, specifically the Segment Anything Model (SAM), under simulated domain shifts in abdominal CT images. The AI approach involves using a systematic slice-level robustness audit of SAM for spleen segmentation in abdominal CT images. The outcome of the study provides insights into the model's robustness and implications for health digital twin deployment.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this study's findings, AI practitioners can use a standardized ground-truth-derived bounding-box protocol to isolate encoder robustness from prompt uncertainty in their own medical image segmentation models. By doing so, they can evaluate the robustness of their models under clinically realistic domain shifts and improve their performance.
case_studies.monetisation: The study's findings can be monetized by developing more robust medical image segmentation models that can be deployed in real-world clinical settings, potentially leading to improved patient outcomes and cost savings. A concrete business opportunity could be to develop a software product that utilizes the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for spleen segmentation in abdominal CT images and sells it to healthcare providers.

case_studies.title: Network Impact of Post-Quantum Certificate Chain sizes on Time to First Byte in TLS Deployments
case_studies.abstract: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) is a rapidly growing deployment challenge as cryptographically relevant quantum computers (CRQC) continue to advance, leaving traditional cryptographic algorithms used in X.509 vulnerable to attack. However, PQC introduces significant deployment challenges in real-world networks, with handshake sizes increasing from 5x to over 20x compared to classical algorithms. In this work, we evaluate the time to first byte (TTFB) under CDN-focused TLS conditions to characterize the latency cost of transitioning existing internet infrastructure to quantum-safe certificate s
case_studies.summary: The problem of transitioning existing internet infrastructure to quantum-safe certificates is a pressing concern due to the vulnerability of traditional cryptographic algorithms to quantum computer attacks. The authors evaluate the time to first byte under CDN-focused TLS conditions to characterize the latency cost of this transition, using post-quantum cryptography (PQC) to assess the impact on network performance. The outcome of this study provides insights into the deployment challenges of PQC in real-world networks, highlighting the significant increase in handshake sizes compared to classical algorithms.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the findings of this study, AI practitioners should consider the latency cost of transitioning to quantum-safe certificates and evaluate the impact on their network performance, taking into account the increased handshake sizes and potential deployment challenges. By doing so, they can develop strategies to mitigate the effects of PQC on their systems and ensure a smooth transition to quantum-safe cryptography.
case_studies.monetisation: The findings of this study present a business opportunity for companies to develop and provide solutions that can efficiently deploy and manage quantum-safe certificates, reducing the latency cost and minimizing the impact on network performance. By offering such solutions, companies can help organizations transition to PQC and stay ahead of the quantum threat, creating a new revenue stream and establishing themselves as leaders in the field of quantum-safe cryptography.

case_studies.title: Feasible-First Exploration for Constrained ML Deployment Optimization in Crash-Prone Hierarchical Search Spaces
case_studies.abstract: Deploying machine learning models under production constraints requires joint optimization over model family, quantization scheme, runtime backend, and serving configuration. This induces a hierarchical mixed-variable search space in which many configurations are invalid: evaluations may crash, exceed memory limits, or violate latency constraints. Standard black-box optimizers such as Tree-structured Parzen Estimators (TPE) and constrained Bayesian optimization are effective when valid configurations are common, but they can spend a large fraction of a small evaluation budget on invalid or uni
case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying machine learning models under production constraints is addressed, where many configurations are invalid due to crashes, memory limits, or latency constraints. The proposed AI approach, Feasible-First Exploration, aims to optimize the deployment of machine learning models in hierarchical search spaces with invalid configurations. The outcome of this approach is to reduce the evaluation budget spent on invalid configurations and improve the overall optimization process.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this approach by first identifying the feasible configurations in the search space and then performing optimization, rather than using standard black-box optimizers that may waste evaluations on invalid configurations. By doing so, practitioners can improve the efficiency of their machine learning model deployment process.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed approach can be monetized by developing a product that automates the deployment optimization process for machine learning models, targeting companies that require efficient and reliable model deployment. This product can be sold as a software solution or a service, offering customization and support for various production environments and model types.
